specification.problem: Compare quantum search by discrete-time and continuous-time quantum walks on a graph with marked vertices, where oracle query cost is counted separately from walk-step cost; the abstract claims that allowing multiple walk steps per query gives a discrete-time walk that matches the continuous-time runtime, a cubic speedup over the classical random walk.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Only generic background definitions are provided: a tiny 4-vertex complete-graph search instance with standard continuous-time search Hamiltonian H=-gamma L-|w><w| and a discrete-time walk step W with oracle O, plus the abstract's speedup-exponent relations stated symbolically. The paper's specific graphs, walk-step counts, runtime formulas, and proofs are outside scope and not reconstructed.

symbols.meaning: quantum walk query time (counting only oracle queries/time)

symbols.domain: positive integer (N=4 in the toy instance)
N x N real symmetric matrix
unitary on C^N (or an extended space)

symbols.meaning: number of walk steps per oracle query

equations.label: Continuous-time search Hamiltonian
equations.description: Standard continuous-time quantum walk search dynamics where the oracle term is applied continuously and only the evolution time counts as query cost.
equations.justification: Standard Childs-Goldstone style formulation; the abstract names continuous-time walks but gives no Hamiltonian.
assumptions: Oracle is the projector onto the marked vertex
Specific graph and gamma are not given in the abstract

equations.label: Discrete-time walk with m steps per query
equations.description: Discrete-time search where m walk steps are interleaved between oracle calls; k queries are counted while the m walk steps per query are not charged.
equations.abstract_quote: we allow the discrete-time quantum walk to also take multiple walk steps per oracle query while only counting queries
equations.justification: The abstract describes multiple walk steps per oracle query; the product form is a natural formalization but the actual schedule is not given.
assumptions: O and W are fixed unitaries
m may depend on the graph

equations.label: Oracle reflection
equations.description: Phase oracle marking the vertex w.
equations.justification: Common discrete-time search oracle form; not stated in the abstract.

equations.label: Quadratic speedup relation for each model with its classical walk
equations.description: Both the discrete-time (one step per query) and continuous-time walks achieve a quadratic speedup over the corresponding classical random walk.
equations.abstract_quote: both achieve quadratic speedups over their corresponding classical random walks
equations.justification: Quadratic speedup is interpreted as square-root scaling; the abstract states no formula, and the continuous-time and discrete-time classical baselines may differ.
assumptions: Speedup interpreted asymptotically in the sense of Theta or O
T_{cl} denotes the respective classical random walk time

equations.label: Cubic speedup relation for multi-step discrete walk
equations.description: Cubic speedup of the discrete-time walk with multiple steps per query, counting only queries, over its classical random walk.
equations.abstract_quote: such that it is a cubic speedup over its corresponding classical random walk
equations.justification: Cubic speedup interpreted as cube-root scaling in query count; exact definition and the relation to the continuous-time runtime are not given.
assumptions: Only queries counted, not walk steps

registers.name: vertex
registers.size: ceil(log2 N) qubits (2 qubits for N=4)
registers.role: position register encoding vertex index in computational basis; basis state |v> for v in {0,...,N-1}

specification.initial_state: Uniform superposition |s> = N^{-1/2} sum_v |v> over vertices (assumed; for discrete walks on edges a coin register may be needed).

steps.description: Prepare the initial state |s> on the vertex register.
Continuous-time variant: evolve under H for time t of order the search time and count only t as cost.
Discrete-time variant: repeat k times the sequence of one oracle call followed by m walk steps.
Compare the resulting query scalings to the classical random walk time as stated in the abstract.

specification.measurement: Measure the vertex register in the computational basis and check whether the outcome is the marked vertex w.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Verify the measured vertex with one oracle call; repeat on failure.
assumptions: No scope was provided; the smallest useful construction chosen is a generic search-by-walk template on a tiny N=4 instance.
Equations eq_1 and eq_3 are textbook background and not claimed to be the paper's constructions.
Speedup exponents are interpreted asymptotically from the abstract's wording.
